senses.definition: A number written with a whole number and a fraction next to it to show their sum.
senses.example: Two and one half is a mixed number.

senses.definition: In usual school examples with positive parts, a fraction whose top number is at least as large as its bottom number.
senses.example: Seven thirds is an improper fraction that means two wholes and one third.

senses.definition: A bottom number that can be used for two or more fractions without changing their values.
senses.example: Six is a common denominator for one half and one third because they can be written as three sixths and two sixths.

senses.definition: A decimal whose digits eventually repeat the same pattern without end.
senses.example: One third is a repeating decimal with a three in every place after the decimal point.

senses.definition: A comparison that gives the amount of one thing for one unit of another.
senses.example: Six eggs for three dollars gives a unit rate of two eggs per dollar.

senses.definition: A way to write a whole number greater than one as prime numbers multiplied together.
senses.example: The prime factorization of 18 is two times three times three.

senses.definition: The largest positive whole number that divides evenly into each of two or more given positive whole numbers.
senses.example: The greatest common factor of six and 15 is three.

senses.definition: The smallest positive number that is a multiple of each of two or more given positive whole numbers.
senses.example: The least common multiple of three and four is 12.

senses.definition: How far a number is from zero on a number line.
senses.example: Negative seven is seven units from zero, so its absolute value is seven.

senses.definition: A rule that says swapping two numbers being added or multiplied leaves the answer the same.
senses.example: By the commutative property, five times eight equals eight times five.

senses.definition: A rule that says changing which numbers you group first in addition or multiplication leaves the answer the same.
senses.example: The associative property lets us add the last two numbers in six plus seven plus three first.

senses.definition: A rule that lets you multiply the parts of a sum or difference separately, then put the results back together.
senses.example: By the distributive property, four times 12 equals four times ten plus four times two.

senses.definition: A number you get by multiplying a whole number by itself.
senses.example: Thirty-six is a square number because six times six is 36.

senses.definition: The number zero or greater named by the square root symbol. Multiplying it by itself gives the number under the symbol.
senses.example: The square root of 49 is seven.

senses.definition: The number you multiply each length by to make a same-shape copy a different size or keep it the same size.
senses.example: With a scale factor of three, a two-inch line on the original is six inches long on the copy.

senses.definition: A picture of how a whole amount is divided, drawn as slices of a circle.
senses.example: The busiest day took up the biggest slice of our pie chart.

senses.definition: A graph that uses pictures or symbols to represent numbers.
senses.example: The key on our pictograph says one moon picture stands for five books.
